Lazer O2 Helmet: White/Red; XL/2XL fits (61-64cm) I just received this from my wife as a Christmas gift. I have gone on 3 rides ranging from 20-60 miles and this helmet is great. A few months ago I went into my favorite local bike shop asking about helmets because I seem to have an unusually large head......yea, a mellon head. Most of the helmets I've tried were too small, too heavy, straps ran weird and uncomfortable, or just plain SQUARE. The Lasor O2 fit like no other helmet I've ever tried. This summer I started useing a "halo" sweat band and I have no problem with the fit, even with my huge mellon head. The unique helmet features a "adjustment dial" that will fine tune the fit to your head with laser percision. This helmet is much lighter than my old Bell I used to wear. You might not notice this on a 10-20 mile ride but if you ride any longer distances you will feel it. During the summer months, I live in Michigan, I try to do one century a month and ...BOY, I can hardly wait to do my first one this year. Another very important feature about this helmet is ....IT LOOKS COOL!! Even my niehbor who likes to make fun of cyclists because of there "pointy hats" said this one looks cool.

Don't look at another helmet. This is the best I've EVER worn. If you cycle a lot, don't hesitate. It's a bit more money but for the serious cyclist it's worth every penny. I try to ride at least 100 mile a week during the good months. If you ride simply with a family or short distances you might want to concider a cheaper model.....unless you have a big fat mellon head like me.
text_fidelity_b: Lazer O2 Helmet: White/Red; XL/2XL fits (61-64cm)

text_fidelity_a:
Levi's Men's 2-Horse Graphic Tee I decided to rate this 4-stars DESPITE getting the wrong “version” which would’ve dropped it to 3-stars.

I had requested the “(New) Dress Blues” version (red print on dark blue); I ended up with the “: (New) Mineral Black” (white print on black). And, honestly? I LOVE the version I got instead. Definitely more clear and bold.

Definitely comfy too.

So, if I like the print style and the comfort, why 4-stars?

THE FIT.

I’m a plus-size girl, so I tend to wear bigger clothes. And, for a gal that wears a 3XL? This fits my frame 100% perfectly. No slouch, no overages, nothing “boxy”.

Why is that a problem?

This is a MEN’s PLUS-SIZE. It shouldn’t FIT like a LADIES 3XL. I know because when I’d buy “mens” (or unisex) t-shirts at souvenir places or the racetracks – the 3XL versions would always be BIGGER than the women’s versions. Also, the “cut” would be more “boxy” for the lack of a better term.

This had a more “ladies” cut/style to it.

It is also shorter than the usual MENS style. This fit rather “short” for a guy, but perfect on my LADIES’ body – almost like it was for a girl.

It had ALL the LEVIs tags – the country/care tag, price tag, side tag, and even the “screen print” neck tag. So, definitely a genuine article.

Perhaps it was a “unicorn” (rare) shirt or how the t-shirt are being designed.

If you’re a BIGGER guy and need a long, boxy, big tee – I wouldn’t recommend this.

If you’re a bigger gal that wants a well-fit, slim, and shorter tee – I’d definitely get this.
text_fidelity_b: Levi's Men's 2-Horse Graphic Tee

text_fidelity_a:
EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit Wow..!! You’re looking at a small sized all-inclusive survival kit that really packs a punch! For the sake of not being redundant and listing included items (see photo I used with the list!) This kit albeit tiny in stature, really holds those basic “urgent” items.. just like circus clowns fit in a toy car!! The overall footprint is perfectly small!! No bigger then, a standard 3x5 notecard- Which makes it a great option to easily tuck inside your gear bag, backpack, tackle box, car glovebox, prepper supplies, etc. Best part of all, when added to a bag- this is so light, you won’t even know it’s there! Mission accomplished.

Love the container- its reminiscent of an old fashion sardine can but, with a useable lid to keep it securely closed.. Fact- the container itself is a working piece to this kits overall function! Giving a lot of thought into keeping this minimal. Of course, being this small in size- you should expect this is just for emergent necessities. This couldn’t sustain a person more than a crisis and certainly wouldn’t suffice for multiple people needs. Items included come in increments of x1 (bandaids = x5) So, if traveling in a group for more then a day.. I’d suggest a larger kit or, at the very least supplement this one.. This has the ability to get you out of a tight spot and would say that’s it’s intended purpose!

Note: One thing I’d definitely recommend with this kit.. and can’t stress enough- is including a simple how too handbook or, guide sheet to take with Ha! Starting a fire with flint isn’t like flicking a switch! If emergent scenario.. it’s safe to assume, the situation is not ideal! So, if ever found in position to use.. it makes sense to have that helpful 411. It may be difference of life/death. (Wow.. I sounded like Dirty Harry just then- ha ha..!!)

If you are prepping for serious situations that could present in your circumstances.. One must also acquire a full first aid kit, food/water supply, Shelter- to subsidize an item like this. BUT, hopefully that is common sense if you’re truly thinking through being prepared!

A few simple adds to make this more complete: Safety pin, small bic lighter (bc, I saw in a post- fire is harder to start then, one might guess- oh, wait.. that was me!) I clipped onto this case a carabiner with a built-in flashlight!! Just those few little items can beef this up a bit. (would have loved to see them included with the set.)

Overall, this is made to avoid being caught empty-handed and could definitely step up to that task 100%. At this price point- this is a great gift for those who love to venture out into situations where they may find themselves needing to be prepared- this will do just that!! I hope this info can help in your decision.. feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit

text_fidelity_a: Pajar Women's Gaetana Boot I literally researched for weeks before buying these. My criteria was the following: good traction, lined with fleece for warmth, removable footbed, waterproof, hits mid calf and I could drive in without it being too clunky. I didn't hear the greatest reviews on Sorels so I honed in on this brand since it's from Canada and they understand Winter essentials. I wear a 9 and it fits true to size, even with heavy socks. (9.5 would've been too big I think) At first I wasn't keen on tying my boots everytime I walked the dog but I could easily slip these on without tying these up.  I wore these straight out of the box and fell in love right away. (no break in period) The color isn't stark white, it's more of an eggshell or offwhite.. super cute. The entire boot is lined in the fleece and has kept my feet warm in 5 degree weather. I will say that my toes do get a tad bit cold when it's in the negatives but it's not a deal breaker since we're not having a typical Winter. I also liked the fact that you can take the top 1/2 of the boot and fold it down, exposing the fleece and wear it that way. When you live in a cold climate, investing in quality pieces are essential-even if you're spending a little more. Try these out, I think you'll be pleasantly surpised. :)
text_fidelity_b: Pajar Women's Gaetana Boot

text_fidelity_a:
Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update) Picked up this tent after LOTS of searching and watching reviews. This tent is heavier than what I wanted for backpacking, however, I think the trade offs will be positive.
First off, the construction is very good out of the bag. All seams and tie out points are sealed with seam tape. No loose threads. The fly and tub are manufactured with a nice weight nylon, not too thin, and not too thick.
The newly designed corner sleeves for the poles are nice, this helps to pull the tent body nice and taut. Great design.
I like the color scheme as well, not too bright, but not drab either.
The aluminum pole segments seem to be shorter than most other tents, this should make it easy to pack in my back pack. I still have not decided if I will roll everything up in the storage bag and pack it vertically. Or use a stuff sack and shove the tent in the bottom of my pack and store the poles on the outside of the pack.
The vestibule is nice. It is not huge, but, it has plenty of room for shoes and some other items that you do not want to store in the tent. The ONE thing that sold me on this tent, is the way the vestibule zips open and closed. The last dome style I had with a vestibule, it zipped right down the middle. This made it hard to get to, as you had to basically crawl most of the way out of the tent to unzip it. This vestibule unzips right at the side of the entrance, which makes it super easy to open and close! AWESOME design!! More tent manufacturers need to use this design.
The only two cons I have right out of the packaging, is:
1. The tent IS on the heavy side, at almost 5 pounds. But, if you were backpacking with a friend or spouse, you could split up the pieces and make it lighter. But for a solo hiker, it is heavy. However, with the room you get, it is a good trade off.
2. The fly tie downs were just short loops of cordage that did not even reach the ground, and you cannot use the stakes to stake them out. Both sides and the rear are like this. I fixed this issue by just adding a length of cordage to all 3 spots.
I removed the supplied plastic line adjusters and just tied a taut line hitch on all pieces of cordage.
I will update after a few uses if need be.
text_fidelity_b: Kelty Grand Mesa Backpacking Tent (2020 Update)

text_fidelity_a:
Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown I was looking forward to having found a good camera here, but disappointed. Similar to a sister company's Primos 02 camera that I tried, I found that the field of the motion sensor was misaligned with the field of the picture. I determined this by walking past the camera to observe the results. Consequently, animals to the right of the picture field of view would set it off and you might not get them in a picture at all. And animals walking from left to right would not trigger it until well past center of the picture. The Primos 02 misalignment was worse but the Bushnell wasn't good.

On the positive, the pictures and videos from this camera were very good; superior to the Primos 02 and another camera I tried. The wide screen picture was perfect for my use. The settings allow for both shutter speed and LED intensity which certainly should be useful to adjust for how far away your primary target area is. It is because of the picture quality that I thought I had found the right camera for me. The Hybrid feature to take both pictures followed by videos is great. Unlike the Primos 02, I didn't have excessive false positive pictures.

But then, I changed the shutter speed and LED settings to take pictures on a closer target area which resulted in the camera taking pictures and videos constantly, nearly 1000 in a 24 hour period. If the "Field Scan" were set to ON, that might have been the result but I had it set to OFF. Of course, two days of this drained the batteries.

Another difficulty is that when set to take three burst pictures, the delay was too quick. Per the time stamp, all three would snap within a single second and you cannot adjust this. So your animal hardly had any time to move further through the field of view.

The camera came with current firmware, so an older version firmware was not to blame for these issues. Possibly the product was defective but I returned it for refund rather than exchange, largely because with my Primos 02 experience an exchange of cameras did not fix the misalignment.
text_fidelity_b: Bushnell 14MP Trophy Cam HD Aggressor Low Glow Trail Camera, Brown

text_fidelity_a:
Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster I wanted to try a drop leg holster for some time and came across this model in desert camo through another vendor. For the price, and because I had heard good things about Fox, I decided to take advantage of the reduced price and see how good (or bad) this holster really is.

The first day, after strapping it on and making all the adjustments I could, I carried around a mini ball peen hammer just to try to get used to it. Why did I choose a hammer? While I am CCW licensed, Florida does not currently allow "open carry". So I had to put something of measurable weight in the holster without alarming the neighbors or anyone driving by on our street. I could imagine someone seeing me with a drop leg holster and calling our local law enforcement, not knowing that their was no gun in the holster -- but assuming there was.Yes, the weight of the hammer head made the holster cant backwards, so I switched to a rubber mallet. This provided a much better balance.

Then I switched to a Glock 23 and a Springfield XD-45 MOD 2 and alternately carried both around inside our home, After trying my darndest to get it to fit properly, I came to the following conclusions:

1. This is a cool looking and well constructed rig. The desert camo design is well done, the material is light and flexible, and the various
clips, belts and fasteners work like they should.
2 The holster accommodated both the Springfield and Glock perfectly and the strap easily fastened over the gun butt.
3. It is very light and designed to fit comfortably against your thigh.
4. And of course it easily carries a lighter weight weapon like a Kahr PM9 and a Glock 42. In fact the smaller and lighter pistols eliminate
the bounding around explained below. But who wants to carry a "pocket pistol" in a drop leg holster?

But, and this is a "big but" for me, the single strap that fastens the holster around your thigh just couldn't keep the holster secure and steady. It bounced while walking and really moved around when running (even at my slow pace). I tightened the thigh strap so that over 14" of strap was outside the buckle, but it just never felt secure. No one wants that feeling -- you want your gun to be right where it's supposed to be -- all of the time.

This holster really needs two improvements: 1. It needs a second strap to go around the thigh, one high and one low. 2. It also needs more vertical adjustment so that it can be carried a bit higher on your belt. Both of these changes would result in a better fit and should eliminate excess movement.
text_fidelity_b: Fox Outdoor Products Mission Ready Drop Leg Holster

I've been using them for years - at least 10 years - the brownish kind that's labeled "Micro Mag". I've never had a single problem with them and I prefer them over the 3414 soft plastic white ones, although these are slightly heavier than the 3414's. When I want to just carry one little kit in my vest or pocket, these are perfect. I've accidentally dropped them on hard surfaces without any breakage or cracks. Of course, I'm sure there's a limit to how much abuse they will take, but if you're careful with your fishing gear there should be no problem.

Since I gave two of them away to my son and wife, I needed a replacement. I tried to consolidate all of my trout gear into one, but found I could be a little more organized with two. I use one for all my terminal tackle, hooks and weights (separated by size) and I'll use the other one for all my lures. The problem I have with the white 3414 box is that the lids don't seal tightly. Every one I've ever had or inspected on the shelf has the same issue. The lids are slightly bowed out. So, when you put a bunch of tiny #14 hooks, swivels, and the like, they always end up migrating to another section. Really irritating. That NEVER happens with the hard 3214.

When I saw these green ones (I've never seen them in the stores), I thought it was perfect. I like the color and it differentiates between my brown one. Comparing it to my old brown one, it is exactly the same - except mine is not labeled Micro Mag like in the picture. The top is just kind of plain with a small Plano logo. I actually prefer this because it makes seeing the contents easier.

As far as all the complaints with the latches not catching, I have NO idea what that's all about. I've handled dozens of these things and never seen that problem, nor have I ever gotten one that didn't work perfectly. You'd have to have pretty poor quality control to let so many go out into the market as seem to be reported, and I personally think Plano has pretty good QC.

BROADREAM Dinosaur Toys Headlamp, T-Rex Kids Dinosaur Toys for Girls Boys Camping, Hiking, Reading in Dark,3 Bright Illumination Modes, Loud Dino Roars, Great Kid Toys Dinosaurs, Christmas, BD Gift [[VIDEOID:2187373aca733f879c0dd8e6a9bc255]] This a fun headlamp designed primarily for kids who like dinosaurs and adventure.

The LED lamp is housed inside a rather large plastic T. rex head. You turn it on by squeezing the open jaws together slightly. The moderately bright light comes on, the eyes light up red, and the dinosaur makes several loud roaring sounds (see attached video). Another squeeze of the jaws and the light turns off.

The adjusable headstrap is decorated with stylized reptilian footprints, in a color scheme that suggests lizard scales. There's a strap down the middle that rides on top of the wearer's head, in addition to the band that goes around your head, to support the weight of the dinosaur and its electronics.

I like that the unit comes with AAA batteries installed. Just pull out the plastic strip that keeps the unit shut off in its package, and it's ready to go. The original batteries probably won't last long, so plan to replace them, preferably with NiMH rechargeables, if you or your young explorers will be using the headlamp much.

This lamp is intended to be a functional novelty, something between a toy and a tool. It doesnt have the brightest light or the most durable housing, among available headlamps, and I'd advise against testing its ability to resist water, especially submersion. The roaring noise could be annoying if someone is trying to use the lamp in a dark room or tent when others are trying to sleep. I do wish that there was some way to turn off the sound. The sound effects may be useful, though, for parents keeping tabs on their young explorer's nighttime activities.

The colorful stripes and loud roar are fanciful embellishments that will likely appeal to young explorers, but I doubt that anyone would defend them as accurate or realistic. Neither of those features are preserved in the fossil record that we have for dinosaurs, so we probably can't say they are inaccurate, either. The thing is intended to fun. Just go with it.

Let me know if anything in my review was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: BROADREAM Dinosaur Toys Headlamp, T-Rex Kids Dinosaur Toys for Girls Boys Camping, Hiking, Reading in Dark,3 Bright Illumination Modes, Loud Dino Roars, Great Kid Toys Dinosaurs, Christmas, BD Gift

However, what I used instead, a 16-ounce glass bottle, was a problem because the bottle is heavy and could potentially break, and it wasn't allowed at the gym. Fortunately, these plastic bottles are 100% BPA free.

I also very much like the bright colors they come in. The blue is very nice, and I plan to get a red one, too.

The bottles are well constructed, too. The bite valve allows for a decent flow of liquid, and its flip mechanism is made of rubber, which doesn't break. It was a bit stiff initially, but it is loosening up as I use it. You have to bite the valve to drink, but I don't mind that.

I own stainless steel straws, so I already have a bottle brush on hand, but you could also purchase the [[ASIN:B00CMOUKJ8 Camelbak Bottle Brush Kit]]. I would personally never let any reusable straw, attached or detached, go without regular cleaning in order to prevent mold buildup, which is toxic.

Note that the straw and rubber bit valve can snap off for cleaning, and the bottle itself can go in the dishwasher.

CFF 4.4 lb Weighted Gloves - 2.2 lbs each. Perfect for Turbo Jam, Beach Body, HIIT, and P90X workouts So I returned the reebok 2lb wrist weights with the thumb hole because they were too big for my wrists. I then thought that perhaps weighted gloves would be better. Problem is that all the weighted gloves out there have their weight distributed only in the back of the hand. I liked that in the picture these looked like the weight wrapped around evenly on both the back and front of the hand.

Well, on me they are definitely more like wrist weights. They do not cover the bottom of my hand like in the picture, but rather go much lower onto my wrist. I think a person with larger hands would make the gloves go up higher towards the hands, but they would definitely need to make the thumb hole a little bigger. text_fidelity_a: CamelBak Eddy Kids Vacuum Insulated Stainless Steel Bottle 12 oz,  Stainless My husband and I have used Camelbak bottles for over 15 years, and we both still use our insulated stainless bottles that are 9 years old. Our kids have been using the camelbak kids bottles for the past 2 years, and while I don’t believe a perfect kids water bottle exists, these are my favorite option. The main problem I’ve seen with camelbak kids bottles is that my 2 and 3 year old chew on the bite valve, which cause it to split wider than it should, then drip when the valve is open and it’s laying on its side. I have probably purchased 8 replacement bite valves for their bottles in the past 2 years because they only seem to last us 6 months or so before the leaking gets out of control. Thankfully Amazon sells 4 packs of replacement valves. If your kid is older and doesn’t chew on it as much, or even if they shut the valve after taking a drink, then that shouldn’t be an issue. Overall I like the camelbak design and I can clean it really well using a bottle brush and straw cleaner. As far as this stainless option goes, it is obviously more prone to being dented and banged up. We already have a nice gouge in the side after being dropped from 2 feet on to tile. But it will keep drinks cold for pretty much the whole day if you give it a few cubes of ice, and there won’t be condensation on the bottle. I love that I can put ice in this and not worry about it making a condensation puddle on my coffee table! I will happily take the dents in exchange for cold water all day long.

text_fidelity_a:
HD101 4 Reticle Tactical Hunting Red/Green Dot Sight Tactical Reflex Rifle Scope with 20mm Rail Mounted on a Ruger 10/22 takedown SS, started at 25 and worked progressively all the way back to 75 yards. Love the different types of reticles, for close work, the round one is my fav as it fits perfectly around the 25 yards target. For medium range I go with the cross hairs, and at 75 it's the dot. I've got a cow bell that got rung at 75 yards as many times as it got shot at - if that's not accurate for a red dot, I don't know what is. I was considering dripping a drop of epoxy on each corner (something I do with most of my $50 under reflex sights, but for this one I decided to leave it alone. After couple of times at the range, the glass gasket is still firmly in place - maybe I got a winner. I also like that they put a bit of thought in the design, as yes, it is silver, but the back housing (where the laser is) has a black top which minimizes glare - smart. So if someone had said - $20 and you got your self a keeper, I'd've said, ur kidding!

UPDATE:
Ooooooops... second outing. Didn't hold zero. Zero at holding zero (sorry, I had to). All of a sudden, I'm getting this jumps, vertically, horizontally. Try to adjust, then boom - it switches up 5 inches high at 50, boom you're now 3 inches to the left. Kept jumping all over the place. Right there and then, I put a zero on its life - it's at the bottom of a trash can. Look, if you LOVE wasting time and money, GET THIS! Otherwise, buy youself some good quality icecream for $20 - it'll be a MUCH better investment.
text_fidelity_b: HD101 4 Reticle Tactical Hunting Red/Green Dot Sight Tactical Reflex Rifle Scope with 20mm Rail

My husband usually mountain bikes when we are camping and my boxer (dog) and myself spend most of our time out hiking the trails and just enjoying nature. I knew when the mud was so bad the last time that I was going to find me a hiking pole. I knew it would have to be very light weight and collapsible since I would want to carry it on or in my camelback until we got to the trails.

This walking/hiking stick is great. It is very light weight as it is a carbon fiber pole with a tungsten steel pole tip. It comes with 3 different guards, 1 is for walking, 1 is for mud and 1 is for snow.The pole is adjustable from 25" to 53' which is very nice and the inside is marked with cm making it very easy for you to remember the size that worked for you the best. It has 2 quick locks that hold it in place, reminds me of my tripod latches. The wrist strap is adjustable to give u a good fit for your grip and it is also padded. The hand grip section is very nice it is made from EVA foam and it is made to absorb your sweat so you don't slip when holding it. It is formed for your fingers and hold giving you a great grip. This does come in a 1 pack or a 2 pack and since I will be holding my dogs leash in 1 hand I only needed 1 pole. I was lucky to get this on sale.
text_fidelity_b: Enkeeo Carbon Fiber Hiking Walking Trekking Pole Ultralight Collapsible Trail Walking Stick with Comfortable EVA Hand Grips, Quick Lock, 25''-53'' Adjustable Length (Black and Orange, 1 Pack)

text_fidelity_a:
ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large We have company coming this summer. This involves a few tents, but one of the people needs an inflatable mattress and room for stuff. This tent is who we got this for.

ASSEMBLY
Assembly was not difficult in our trial run. The instructions were pretty easy to follow and it does not take more than a half hour to put up with two people unless you are with someone VERY efficient in putting up tents.

WITHOUT FLY
Without the fly, this is a very nice tent - bright, airy, and lots of upper mesh to see the sky. This is perfect on nice days.

WITH FLY
The days that rain might be expected are the challenge. The fly is dark blue. The dark blue makes this tent feel very warm and almost oppressive some days, but it does protect in the rain. My point is if you are the type who does not want to take the fly off and put it on constantly, this might be a big dark for you to leave on constantly, unless you plan to just sleep inside and don't care.

STAKES
The stakes that come with this are not big enough to support the weight of wind and other frustrations. We got spiral stakes to use with this at least on the key points of stress and it works better.

STURDY?
We are only using this for this summer, so hopefully it will last through several weeks of use. We have not had any high winds or severe storms yet so I will have to update as to how well this worked for that.

STORM PROOFING
One thing we learned about tents over long term is that double tarps are a good idea. We put one down under the tent leaving a perimeter that is not too big around the edge. Then we put another inside the tent to further protect should there be a deluge.

STORAGE
I find that having a separate nylon bag for the fly helps a lot when it comes time to put this tent away. It allows for a faster pick up time and less frustrating trying to make everything fit.

SIZE
This is perfect for a queen sized mattress, 1 or 2 people and their stuff.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is great for a family with sleeping bags and not much stuff, or for less people and more stuff. The stakes could be better, the storage bag bigger, and perhaps a bit tougher construction/fabric, but all in all this is a decent tent and serves our purpose well- I hope.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS at this point. I will update once summer is over as to the longevity of this tent over several weeks.
text_fidelity_b: ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large

WINNINGO Portable Bike Floor Pump Every cyclist needs to carry a portable pump and an extra tube with them at all times. If you happen to get a flat ten miles away from your home, you are out of luck. You can't try to ride on a flat tire because it's dangerous and you'll ruin both the tire and the rim. It's a much better practice to have a high quality pump.

This Winningo portable pump is a perfect choice. The gauge takes out the guesswork and you can use this pump to get back to your regular tire pressure and continue with your ride. The valve can easily be converted between Presta and Schrader. The valve is attached to a rubber tube which makes inflation a lot more convenient. Many portable pumps attach directly to the valve stem, and if you're not careful you can accidentally snap off the stem when you inflate. The rubber tube makes that unfortunate outcome virtually impossible.

This portable pump is designed like a mini floor pump. It stands upright and a foot pedal flips out for stability. This allows you to pump up your tire with the assistance of body weight. You can easily inflate a tire to its recommended pressure with this pump, but the pump is compact enough to fit on a clip beside a water bottle cage on the downtube. This is a great product that will ensure you are well equipped to get back out on the road if you ever have a flat during a ride.
text_fidelity_b: WINNINGO Portable Bike Floor Pump

MIER Extra Large Waterproof Duffel Backpack Roll Top Duffle Bags for Men Women 60/100/150L Heavy Duty Dry Bag for Kayaking Boating Camping Gear Motorcycle Trips Hiking Travel Rafting I received the Mier 60L backpack and immediately put it to use on my electric kick scooter. First I transported a huge load of dirty linen for my wife from her massage therapy business to the laundry via scooter (3/4 capacity). Then I swung by Trader Joe's supermarket and loaded up at least 30 lbs of food and scootered home (2/5 capacity).

The Mier backpack performed extremely well. The 60L volume is HUGE. Huuuge. I am 6' tall, 215 lbs, fit. This is ALL you need for standard transport. The 150L (at more than double the volume of the 60L) should be able to hold a body... A use for the 150L would likely be transporting bulky, light loads (e.g., 25 food trays that need to be kept vertical).

These are truly MEGA packs.

If you're working for a food delivery service, and need to use a backpack, this is your product. Super dense, sturdy material. Good strong shoulder straps with reinforced connection points. Padding on the straps is decent for usage in 30 minute stints under max load or all day under light loads. And while not officially listed as insulated, the thickness and type of material makes me think this would be good for food delivery as it should keep in the heat, keep out the cold, and be very easy to keep clean.

The only downside was my back sopping with sweat due to the pack exterior not being made of breathable material.

Highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
[New Arrival] Cocoweb TraiLead 3 Bike Hitch-Mount Bike Rack The rack is solid. Really easy to attach to the hitch. In our case I have to problem whatsoever to attach it when we need it and remove it right after use using the included hardware. One review mentioned that leaves it exposed to a theft, so I tossed a wrench and remove the rack while we are biking (it takes about a minute). Perhaps the greatest feature are those bike cradles and straps. We transport 3 bikes - 1 men frame, 1 women and 1 children's. They all hang at different angles, but all 3 are very solid and unmovable. The collapsible frame is a nice feature too. Once I forgot to close the door while I already had one bike attached to the rack (yeah, I was tired after a long ride :-)) Lowered the rack with that bike on it, closed the door, return the rack back to upright position and kept loading the remaining 2 bikes.

The only (perceived maybe) con of this rack - it is a bit wobbly when it is loaded and the car is moving. When I keep that in mind and drive a bit more carefully that does not appear to be an issue. Note that bikes are attached securely and do not move at all even a little bit relative to each other or to the frame. But the entire thing wobbles slightly left and right when the car moves on an uneven pavement. I do not think this is a hitch connector issue as it fits snugly into a hitch receiver. Could be that the 1.25" to 2" adapter just cannot provide enough support. Or maybe that's the inherent weakness of hitch-mounted racks (the connection to the receiver cannot be rigid enough). Or both... Take into account that this is our first rack and I have no experience whatsoever with other racks. They probably all wobble, I just do not have a good reference to say whether this wobbles more or less.
text_fidelity_b: [New Arrival] Cocoweb TraiLead 3 Bike Hitch-Mount Bike Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell So far, this is a great bell! I just installed it today after I received it in the mail. It looks and fits great on my 2022 Trek Marlin 6. I was in my garage checking out the new bell and ringing it a few times while my wife was about 40 feet away outside in the driveway talking with her friend who was parked in the driveway with her car running and they both said that they could easily hear the bell. Her friend was in her car and my wife was standing outside the car, mind you, that car was not quite with the cooling fans running and the wind was also blowing to create extra noise. Yes, this bell is plenty loud to get someone's attention. This bell also allows you to rotate the dinger in any position you want, which gives you the ability to position exactly where it is best for you. You just rotate the assembly below the bell and put it how you want it. This is a very well thought out design that works great!

Another example later that evening, I was riding down a pathway that parallels the roadway and as I was approaching a parking lot driveway, there were two vehicles stopped waiting to exit to the roadway. I decided to continue down the pathway between the rear of one vehicle and the front of the other vehicle. But just to make sure that the second car saw me coming, I slowed and chimed the bell three times to get her attention as I was approaching about 25 feet away. She looked up and at me, smiled and waved as I slowly rode between the two vehicles. The bell worked as designed. The construction seems to be sturdy, but time will tell. I would recommend this to anyone looking for a small bell that does the job.
text_fidelity_b: Mirrycle Incredibell Original Bicycle Bell

text_fidelity_a:
ANCHEEER 26inch Mountainbike Electric Bike UPDATE: Two years later and I still love it!!

This bike has lots of advantages: It is manageable (I'm 68 and can lift it with some effort), it is a blast to ride on electric, and it's pretty stable and comfortable. I'm definitely glad I bought it, as it gets me outside and gives me exercise I enjoy. But it is not perfect. For one, I had to take it to a bike shop because the brake pads and brake plates didn't line up. No matter how I fiddled with it, the brakes were always applied which made peddling hard. I wish I could say they fixed it, but they were only able to make it better, so peddling is still kind of hard, no matter which gear I am in. The other thing is the peddle-assist. The truth is that no matter how soft or slow you peddle, even on the lowest setting the assist mode will take over and will take you faster than you can peddle. That's fine if you want to go fast, but if you're looking for exercise, you can't use the peddle assist at all. So when I switch it on, I take it off peddle assist mode which allows me to use the grip as a throttle (like on a motorcycle), and I alternate between unassisted peddling, or going without peddling and only using the throttle. I find the latter very useful for taking off from a complete stop, as well as switching into when I am on a rough road or when I start to tire. So I've found a way to make it work for me. But it would have been nice to be able to use the peddle assist mode. The other thing is the adjustables, especially the seat and handlebar height. I find that if I have the adjustment levers loose enough that I can close them, the seat or handlebar just slides down to the lowest level. But if I tighten the lever, I can't close it. So I find I have to stop several times in a trip to readjust the height of either the seat or the handlebar.

I made some adjustments. I found the grip on the peddles too aggressive, so I switched them out for peddles with a less aggressive grip that also fold, which makes it more convenient to store in the car trunk. I cut off the rubber end of one of the handles and inserted a rear view mirror, which, frankly, I don't see how I can live without. I added a softer seat which really helps.

The inconveniences I mentioned are not deal-killers. They are annoyances or disappointments. I still love the bike and would recommend it to anyone who is looking for a fun ride, for exercise, for beating city traffic and avoiding public transportation during Covid. I love that I can peddle as far as I want and still be certain to make it home because I can ride myself back on electric. This freedom is fantastic.
text_fidelity_b: ANCHEEER 26inch Mountainbike Electric Bike

text_fidelity_a:
SURQO Shorty Wetsuits Men and Women 2mm Neoprene Front Back Zip Keep Warm for Surfing Swimming Diving Water Sports This wetsuit is a bit different than others I've had in that it lacks the typical down-the-back zipper. You have a shoulder cowl that fits over your neck, and that zips in place at the front. It flips back like a zippo lighter revealing the opening through which you squeeze your body.

It was a bit snug to squeeze myself into, which you would expect. Once I got my hips where they should be, everything else went smoothly. I'm a very thin framed guy, so my hips are my widest point. If you have a larger belly than hips, you might go for a larger size and then you wouldn't have that problem. I definitely echo another reviewer's advice of finding your largest dimension and using that as your guide, otherwise you may not fit as well. Once I had everything in position, the fit was nice and snug, and there weren't any areas where it pinched. There is also plenty of room between the legs for the boys, so there is no uncomfortable squeezing in that area.

It feels like it would keep you warm in the winter in Florida or California. It would make an excellent rash guard that provides some insulation in warm to slightly chilled, but not bitter cold, conditions.

The upside of having a zipper in front is that it's easy to zip and unzip. However, having the cowl flip back means that it's still very difficult to put on by yourself, unless you have double-jointed shoulders or something. The trouble is reaching the cowl at all when it's located dead center on your back. You need to somehow get the cowl up over your head, at which point the rest is easy to do. If there was a strap or something attached to the cowl, this would make it much easier to do solo. Removing the suit, on the other hand, is easy to do by yourself.

It is definitely more flexible than most wetsuits I've worn, although likely not quite as warm as many. This is clearly designed for California surfers, but it should work just as well for snorkeling, SCUBA, and other recreational activities. And last but not least, the style is simple but smart My wife says that it looks very flattering on me. Overall this is a good suit, and well worth the price.
text_fidelity_b: SURQO Shorty Wetsuits Men and Women 2mm Neoprene Front Back Zip Keep Warm for Surfing Swimming Diving Water Sports

text_fidelity_a:
Repel Umbrella The Original Portable Travel Umbrella - Umbrellas for Rain Windproof, Strong Compact Umbrella for Wind and Rain, Perfect Car Umbrella, Backpack, and On-the-Go I needed an umbrella for an upcoming trip to somewhere and this seemed like a decent buy. More to the point, it would arrive before I was scheduled to depart unlike some of the other choices. It was more than a tad pricey but the reviews were overall favorable so I went for it. Turns out I didn’t need it for that trip because the weather forecasters failed in their job.

Fast forward a few months to an actual winter rainstorm. Rain is coming down at a more-than-irritating rate. Wind is blowing at about 15 MPH with occasional gusts to 25-40. Umbrella is inverting itself about every 40 feet even without the gusts, and I’m not nearly as dry as I was when using my previous cheap Sam Walton special that was great but for the weak fabric. I want to rage-throw this pos across the parking lot, but that would be littering. It didn’t get better on subsequent uses.

Pros:
Mechanism to deploy it is smooth and fast.
If it’s not breezy, it will keep you dry, and do a pretty good job as a parasol on a sunny day (failed me in Puerto Rico’s mild breezes though).
Light weight and compact.

Cons:
It has vents that are supposed to prevent the inversion problem, but they are way too far away from the center to work even a little bit.

Opinion:
Buy it if you have no other option, otherwise avoid at all costs.
text_fidelity_b: Repel Umbrella The Original Portable Travel Umbrella - Umbrellas for Rain Windproof, Strong Compact Umbrella for Wind and Rain, Perfect Car Umbrella, Backpack, and On-the-Go

text_fidelity_a:
iBert Child Bicycle Safe-T-Seat My daughter and I love this seat. I bought it because I did not want to haul a heavy trailer.

It is installed on my beach cruiser and it fits perfectly - plenty of room for me to reach the handlebars and pedal without the bike seat in the way. I am 5'4" short. It was easy to install. I am surprised at how stable and natural it feels.

I bought it when she was 10 months old, but she was too small to use it. I started using it when she was just over 1 yr and she fit much better (she is average size).

So far we do short rides around the neighborhood in the evenings and weekends and I can take her 1.5 miles to daycare, and she loves it. She can also look up and see me and ring the bell. We can talk about the things we see on the ride, unlike if we had a trailer.

She has fallen asleep twice while riding. There is nowhere for her head to go, but to slump sideways. I have just supported her head with my hand for the few minutes it takes me to get home.

One very nice aspect to this seat is that it mounts on the bike stem, so when she grabs the handlebars, she can't get any torque to steer the bike.

Mine came with the padding for the seat.

Cons:
The shoulder straps are a little strange - they can slide off her shoulder, but this won't be a problem when she is bigger.

The bar that comes down over the child's lap has a cheap attachment mechanism. This ought to be fixed in the next models - it is not acceptable for a product this expensive.

In a light rain (like we encountered last weekend), water puddles in the bottom of the foot cups - I might drill a hole on the bottom of each one (we live in the Pacific NorthWest).

text_fidelity_a:
LEM Big Bite Digital Smoker I have ordered 7 40" digital electric smokers this past year from Home Depot (because of their one year return policy using the house credit card). Three MasterBuilt, two Smoke Hollow, and this LEM unit twice. Bluetooth, regular and with RF remote control. All have been returned except for this one.

My original LEM Big Bite was serial #0004. My current one is #0048. My first one registered 40° higher than my external thermometer, blew out the chip tray half way with flames belching out (luckily I was near it at the time to prevent fire to the deck) during the burnin (I had the vents closed) and the not so secured gasket around the door. Scary. ABut on paper it seemed to be the best.

Since I was locked into HD (they just credit your HD credit card for a return), I went through all of their 40" digital electric smokers. With the new season coming, their inventory filled with pellet smoker/grills (I sold my Cookshack Fast Eddy PG 500, wanting to go the electric smoker route. So I took a chance and reordered the LEM.

Holds temperature to within 15° of my external thermometer (which reads higher.) All the other smokers read higher than my external one so basically they could not get to their supposed top temperature (as was evidenced by my cooks not being quite done in the usual time.) So at worst it's hotter inside than the set temp which is easily adjusted for but it may just be the location of my external thermometer vs the builtin one which I rally can't find as yet.

In any case I believe I can trust the temperature I set and use meat probes to determine the end of the cook anyway.

As to the shortfalls, the loose door gasket had not changed. I used some Gorilla glue in a few spots to further adhere the gasket to the door.

I do not use the included chip tray, opting for the Masterbuilt external smoke unit, a 10' dryer hose, 3" metal duct and duct tape to secure the external smoker unit into the slot where the chip tray was. I prefer the cleaner smoke produced with the creosote clinging into the 10' tubing instead of into the smoke profile. To illustrate, three of my smokers had glass doors. Using the chip trays, the glass was orange/brown following a 6 hour smoke. Using the external smoke generator the glass doors remained clear. That's creosote which can leave that tingly feeling on the tip of your tongue.

I keep both vents closed as smoke escapes from them anyway and a small amount from the closed door. (It would be nice it the door latch could be adjusted to be tighter like other smokers provide.) This provides enough air flow to keep the smoke going.

My unit arrived by UPS with some carton tears and a couple of small dents on the rear wall.

I don't need Bluetooth or an rf remote control. The display panel is easily read in bright sunlight. The control buttons are very intuitive, more so than any of my other electric smokers.

It's the keeper and I can stop my search. Not perfect but better than the rest so far. Just hope it lasts. The 5 year warranty might suggest that.

Forgot to mention that there is absolutely no assembly required, not a single screw. Just remove the plastic ties that secure the shelves for shipping. Plug and play.
text_fidelity_b: LEM Big Bite Digital Smoker

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Grunge Board downtube bike fender I've got a bicycle without any mounting holes for fenders. It also doesn't have enough clearance between the forks/brakes and tires to jerry-rig a fender. However, I hate not riding my bike because of light rain or a few puddles.

The Grunge Board was the best option that I could find at a reasonable price. It straps onto the downtube with a couple of rubber straps. I've got an 80s racing bike with tight geometry, and the dimensions of the board are small enough to clear the crankarms and the front wheel during turns. But just so (orientation makes a difference).

I've ridden through some big puddles and it seems to do a fairly good job of keeping my pant legs from getting soaked. I still put some scotch tape over the holes/slits around the bottom bracket to keep the gunk from getting in. The board is light enough that I leave it on all the time, even when it's not raining...just in case there is an unexpected puddle.

I have to take off a star because I think the mounting band should have been designed better. First, it hard to push the rubber bands through the narrow slots once they wrap around the downtube. The bands have slits in them that attach to nubs on the underside of the board. The nubs are not large enough to hold the bands in place perfectly securely. They seem to usually work, but the bands come off occasionally. If you have a small diameter downtube (as in most pre-90s, bikes), there are also a couple inches of extra rubber band that just flop around. It shouldn't be too hard for Planet Bike to redesign this retention mechanism, but it's also hard to complain for ~$10.

You can use a couple of cable ties instead of the rubber bands and they'd probably do a better job. You could also use a large soda bottle cut to size and get the same effect, though arguably a bit uglier.
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Grunge Board downtube bike fender

text_fidelity_a:
JACO MBX-60 Presta Tire Pressure Gauge for Bikes (Max 60 PSI) | MTB & XC Series The old saying that a person who has one watch always knows what time it is, but a person who has two watches is never sure, comes to mind here. If this is your only pressure gauge and you dial in your tire pressures based on this tool, you’ll be happy. But if you have a couple of different gauges like me, some on pumps and another that is independent like this one, then you won’t be exactly sure which one is accurate.

However, consistency and precision is what matters. Based on several years of use and comparison to two other gauges and my car readouts, I trust my digital gauge on my bike floor pump for accuracy from psi ranges in the mid teens to the mid 50s. I took readings from several different pressures as benchmarked with my pump, and this analog gauge consistently read about 1 psi lower. That consistency is more than good enough for me. And by way of background, I’ve set up my mountain bike and gravel bike with tubeless tires, and I am particular about the pressures I run in different conditions.

Also, this gauge has a rubberized face and comes in a sturdy and well padded case. Since this is a precision instrument, I appreciate the protection to keep this device working well.

Overall this is an easy to use tool that feels like it will last a long time (as long as you don’t abuse it).
text_fidelity_b: JACO MBX-60 Presta Tire Pressure Gauge for Bikes (Max 60 PSI) | MTB & XC Series
